info.title: FloodIntel API
info.description: The HTTP contract of the FloodIntel server. It is hand-written from the code and pinned by tests/Feature/ApiContractTest.php: the document must list every route in routes/api.php exactly once, must declare the role or ability its route middleware enforces, and must name the form request that validates the body. Authentication is a Laravel Sanctum bearer token wherever `security` is present. Errors are JSON `{"message": ...}`; a validation failure adds an `errors` object keyed by field, and the photo-size refusal adds `photo_size` beside `photo` (D-108). Any request that declares a body above 6 MiB is answered `413` before routing, and a photo above 5 MiB is answered `422` on `photo` and `photo_size` (API-07). The surface is deliberately unversioned (D-123): every path is under `/api/`, no version segment or version header exists, and `info.version` dates this document rather than the API. Additive changes ship at any time; a breaking change ships with the client in one release, and only a consumer that cannot deploy with the server forces a `/v2`.

tags.description: Sign in, sign out, email verification, and password reset.

post.summary: Sign in and issue an API token
post.description: The identifier is an email address or a contact number. A failed attempt counts against a five-attempt window keyed on the identifier and address; once the window is spent the request answers `429` with `Retry-After`.

200.description: The authenticated account and a new plain-text token.

post.description: The answer is identical whether or not the address is registered. When the mail transport cannot deliver, the request answers `503` instead of claiming a send (fallback row 17).

200.description: The request is accepted for any address.

post.summary: Reset a password with a mailed token
post.description: A successful reset revokes every existing token for the account. The password rule is at least twelve characters with letters and numbers (FR-96).

200.description: The password was reset.

get.summary: Verify an email address from a signed link
get.description: The link is signed and throttled. Without a JSON `Accept` header the request redirects to the frontend with a query flag.

200.description: The address is verified.

302.description: Redirect to the frontend with `?email=verified` or `?email=verification-failed`.

Location.description: The frontend URL carrying the outcome flag.

200.description: The notice.

post.description: Answers `409` when the address is already verified and `503` when the mail transport cannot deliver (fallback row 17).

get.description: The account is returned at the document root, not inside `data`.

200.description: The authenticated account with its barangay.

get.summary: List the reports visible to the caller
get.description: The caller's abilities decide the scope: `view-all-barangays` reads every barangay, `view-own-barangay` reads its own, and anyone else reads only their own reports. `status=validated` is a review-queue filter, not the consumption path; consumers read `/api/flood-reports/validated-feed`. A `barangay_id` filter is ignored for a caller without `view-all-barangays`.

200.description: One page of visible reports, newest observed first.

post.description: A field report carries either an `alert_level` with a `flood_type`, or a legacy `flood_level`; never both. `reported_at` is the observation instant, is required, and is immutable once stored (D-06, D-119). `client_uuid` is the reporter's idempotency key: a second submission with the same key is answered `200` with the stored report and no second row or photo (D-110), while a first submission is answered `201`. A photo above 5 MiB, or one that is not a readable JPEG, PNG, or WebP with a clean container, answers `422`. A photo write that fails answers `503` before any row exists (D-111).

200.description: A replay: the report with this `client_uuid` was already stored, and that report is returned unchanged.

get.description: The detail carries the status history, the correction chain, and the stored address. A caller who cannot see the report is refused `403`, not `404`.

200.description: The report.

post.description: Only a `submitted` report can be validated. A report in any other state answers `422` on `status`.

200.description: The validated report.

post.summary: Return a submitted report for correction
post.description: The returned report can be corrected once; the correction cites it through `supersedes_id`.

200.description: The returned report.

post.description: Rejection is the officer-only route group's (FR-108); the ability it authorizes on is `validate-report`, which staff also hold, so a staff member is refused `403` by the group.

200.description: The rejected report.

post.description: Only a `validated` or `returned` report can be overridden, and only to `validated`, `returned`, or `rejected`.

200.description: The overridden report.

get.description: The window runs cutoff to cutoff (04:00 and 15:00 Asia/Manila, D-24). `pending.basis` names whether any row fell back to its receipt time because it has no observation instant.

200.description: The current window and its per-barangay pending counts.

get.description: This is the consumption path for FR-24: it reads only reports that passed the one `validated` scope, so a consumer never filters status itself. `depth_cm` is null when the report recorded no depth; the derived surface composes the basemap elevation with it (D-78).

200.description: The feed, newest observed first, with a count and a truncation flag instead of pagination.

get.summary: Export the report log as CSV
get.description: The export reads the same filters as the queue, so the two views cannot disagree (FR-29). The photo is a URL cell, never the bytes. The response is streamed in 500-row chunks; `X-Report-Count` states the row count before the stream begins.

200.description: The CSV stream. Columns: report_id, barangay, flood_type, status, status_label, alert_level, alert_level_label, reporter_name, reporter_role, observed_at, received_at, latency_seconds, latitude, longitude, address, depth_cm, notes, photo_url.

X-Report-Count.description: The number of rows the stream will contain.

get.summary: List the flood events still accepting filings

200.description: The open events, newest first.

get.summary: List the impact reports visible to the caller
get.description: The same visibility rule as the level reports; `per_page` is read without a validation rule.

200.description: One page of visible impact reports, newest observed first.

post.description: Only a captain holds `submit-impact-report`. The barangay is the caller's own and is never read from the payload. `individuals` must be at least `families`, and a cited level report must belong to the caller's barangay (D-118). `reported_at` is required and immutable (D-119). `client_uuid` is the idempotency key: a replay answers `200` with the stored report (D-110).

200.description: A replay: the report with this `client_uuid` was already stored, and that report is returned unchanged.

get.description: The closed constraint set, each value with its display label and its note rule (FR-112, NFR-42, D-129). It is the one source of the vocabulary: capture, filters, lists, and any future legend render these labels rather than a copy held by the client. It carries no tag data and no ability gates it, so any authenticated account may read it.

200.description: Every taxonomy value in catalogue order.

get.summary: List the access tags visible to the caller
get.description: Reads are scoped exactly as the report log is (FR-119): the command center reads every barangay, a barangay-scoped account reads its own, and any other account reads only the tags it recorded. `barangay_id` is applied only when the caller may read beyond its own barangay (FR-120). The filter range is on the observation instant, and a retired tag is still readable but reports `is_active` false.

parameters.name: barangay_id
parameters.description: Applied only when the caller may read beyond its own barangay.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Lower bound on the observation instant.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Upper bound on the observation instant.

200.description: One page of visible tags, newest observed first.

post.description: Only the two field roles hold `record-access-tag` (FR-118, D-128). The barangay and the recording account come from the authenticated request and are never read from the payload; an account without a barangay is refused `422` naming `barangay_id` before any row exists (FR-115). `observed_at` is the capture instant and is required, never replaced by the receipt time (FR-114). A note is required when the type is `other` (D-127).

get.description: The view policy applies the same three branches as the list: every barangay, the caller's own, or only what the caller recorded (FR-119).

200.description: The tag.

get.description: The provider budget is shared and a failure is absorbed: an unavailable provider answers `200` with a null address rather than an error, because the address is a convenience and the coordinates are the record (FR-32).

200.description: The translated address, or null when no address could be resolved.

get.description: Superseded rows stay in the table for their reports but are not offered here.

200.description: Every active barangay, ordered by name.

get.description: Read-only: the catalogue is closed (FR-105), so a grant change is a recorded decision rather than a request here. The gate is the `manage-users` ability, not the officer route group (D-114).

200.description: Every role with its interface, scope, and abilities.

get.description: Officer-only. `role` and `barangay_id` filter the list; `per_page` is read without a validation rule.

200.description: One page of accounts, newest first.

post.description: The password rule is at least twelve characters with letters and numbers. A barangay is required for every barangay-scoped role, checked after validation so the error binds to `barangay_id` (FR-107).

patch.description: Every field is optional. An officer cannot change their own role (FR-103); that attempt answers `403`. A role that requires a barangay cannot be left without one.

200.description: The updated account.

delete.description: An officer cannot delete their own account; that attempt answers `403`.

200.description: Every token the account owns. The plain-text value is never returned again.

post.description: The plain-text token is returned once, in `token`; only its hash is stored.

201.description: The stored token and its plain-text value.

204.description: Every token the account owned was revoked, including the one that authorized this request.

get.description: The channel topics are derived from the caller's identity and never read from the request. When Realtime is not configured the answer is `enabled: false` and the client keeps its polling substitute (D-63, D-65).

200.description: The Realtime settings and the caller's topics, or `enabled: false`.

post.description: The report must be visible to the caller. A sample whose latency cannot be computed is stored with a null latency and reported as excluded rather than dropped.

get.description: The window is clamped to 1–168 hours. `excluded` counts samples with no usable instant, so a selective window cannot be presented as a capability (TNFR-05, D-67).

200.description: The median, maximum, bound, and breach count for the window.

sanctum.description: Send the plain-text token from `POST /api/login` or `POST /api/tokens` as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

Signature.name: signature
Signature.description: The signature the signed URL carries.

Expires.name: expires
Expires.description: The signed URL's expiry instant, when the link is time-limited.

SearchTerm.name: q
SearchTerm.description: Case-insensitive match against notes, landmark, address, and the reporter's full name.

ObservedFrom.name: from
ObservedFrom.description: Include reports observed at or after this instant.

ObservedTo.name: to
ObservedTo.description: Include reports observed at or before this instant.

Unauthenticated.description: The request carries no valid Sanctum token.

Forbidden.description: The caller's role or ability does not admit this route, the email address is unverified, or the action's own policy refused it. A policy refusal reads "This action is unauthorized."; the role gate answers with an empty message. The role and ability that apply are stated on each operation.

NotFound.description: No record with that identifier exists, or it is not visible to the caller (the report detail answers `403` for a report it may not read, and `404` only for one that does not exist).

ValidationFailed.description: One or more fields failed validation. `errors` is keyed by field name; the photo size refusal adds `photo_size` beside `photo` (D-108). Nothing is stored.

TooManyRequests.description: A named rate limiter refused the request. The response carries `Retry-After` in seconds.

PayloadTooLarge.description: The declared request body exceeds 6 MiB. The application answers before routing, authentication, or validation (API-07).

example.message: The request body is too large. The limit is 6 MB.

ServiceUnavailable.description: A required dependency — the mail transport or the photo store — could not be reached, so the request is refused rather than answered with a success the infrastructure cannot back (fallback row 17, D-111).

value.message: The reset email could not be sent. Try again later.
The photo could not be stored. Try again later.

token.description: The plain-text Sanctum token. It is returned once and never again.
The plain-text token. It is returned once and never again.

reported_at.description: The observation instant the reporter sent. Null only for a legacy row written before the field was required (D-119).

status_changes.description: Present on the detail and on a decision response; absent from the list and from a fresh submission.

client_uuid.description: The reporter's idempotency key, echoed so a client can match a stored row to its queue record (D-110).

superseded_by_id.description: Present only when the relation is loaded.

supersedes.description: Present only when the relation is loaded.

depth_cm.description: Null when the report recorded no depth; the derived surface composes the basemap elevation with it (D-78).

truncated.description: True when more rows matched than the limit returned.

AccessTagType.description: The closed taxonomy (D-127). A place may carry more than one tag.

requires_note.description: True when the value cannot be understood without a note (FR-112).

AccessTag.description: A constraint on a place (D-124, D-125). It carries no resident, household, medical, or disability field.

type_label.description: The server's display label for the type; the client never renders the raw value.

observed_at.description: The capture instant, never the receipt time (FR-114).

is_active.description: False once retired; a retired tag stays readable (FR-121).

token.description: A short-lived Supabase-compatible JWT. Its subject is the account id.

topics.description: `reports:all`, `reports:barangay:<id>`, and `reports:user:<id>`, derived from the caller's abilities.

login.description: An email address or a contact number.

password.description: At least twelve characters with letters and numbers (FR-96).

alert_level.description: One of the two level spellings. Providing both `alert_level` and `flood_level` is refused.

flood_level.description: The legacy level spelling. A legacy report carries no flood type.

photo.description: The report photo. At most 5 MiB, read as JPEG, PNG, or WebP with a clean container (API-08). Above 5 MiB the answer is `422` on `photo` and `photo_size` (D-108).

reported_at.description: The capture instant, never later than the server clock. Required; the server never substitutes its own clock (D-06, D-119).

client_uuid.description: The reporter's idempotency key, usually the queue record's id or `local-<epoch>-<hex>` (D-110).

supersedes_id.description: The returned report this submission corrects. It must be in the caller's barangay, still returned, and the head of its chain (FR-14).

related_level_report_ids.description: Level reports of the caller's own barangay, at most fifty, without repeats (D-118).

reported_at.description: The capture instant, never later than the server clock; required and immutable (D-119).

supersedes_id.description: The submitted report this correction answers, in the same barangay and event; the head check runs under lock (D-110).

password.description: At least twelve characters with letters and numbers (FR-96).

barangay_id.description: Required when the role is barangay-scoped (FR-107).
